chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: For every salat (prayer) there are two times, and the first of the time is the more excellent of them. And it is not for anyone to make the latter of the two times his time, except in a case of excuse, without illness.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُهُ: the more virtuous or superior of the two
key_terms.عُذْرٍ: a valid excuse that permits delay
key_terms.وَقْتَانِ: two time periods allotted for the prayer

ai.seo_question: Does each salat (prayer) have two valid times, and is praying at the beginning of the time better?
ai.summary: This hadith states that each salat (prayer) has two valid time periods, while emphasizing that performing the prayer at the beginning of its time is more virtuous. It also teaches that delaying to the latter time should not be adopted as a norm except in the presence of an excuse.
